blocks.text: Yeh Unit 2 (Further Differentiation) ke poore unit se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal mukhtasar qadmon mein hal kiya gaya hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Define the derivative of a function \(y = f(x)\). What does it give?
(Function \(y = f(x)\) ke derivative ki definition likhein. Yeh kya batata hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\), agar limit maujood ho. Yeh kisi point par function ki instantaneous rate of change (fori sharah-e-tabdeeli) deta hai, yani wahan tangent ki slope.

book_ref.quote: The derivative gives the instantaneous rate of change of the function at a point.

blocks.prompt:
2 Differentiate \(y = \dfrac{x^{3} + 2}{x - 1}\) with respect to \(x\).
(\(y = \dfrac{x^{3} + 2}{x - 1}\) ka \(x\) ke lihaaz se derivative nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Quotient Rule: This rule is used to differentiate the division of two functions.

blocks.prompt:
3 Find \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\) from the definition (first principles), \(x \ne 0\).
(Definition (first principles) se \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\) nikalein, \(x \ne 0\).)
blocks.explanation: \(h \to 0\) se pehle difference quotient ko simplify karein.

book_ref.quote: We may not put \(h = 0\) straight away: that gives \(\frac{0}{0}\).

blocks.prompt:
4 Differentiate \(y = x^{3}\sin x\) with respect to \(x\).
(\(y = x^{3}\sin x\) ka derivative nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Product rule: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2}\sin x + x^{3}\cos x = x^{2}(3\sin x + x\cos x)\).

book_ref.quote: The derivative of the sine function is the cosine function

blocks.prompt:
5 Simplify and then differentiate \(y = \dfrac{1 + \tan x}{\sec x}\).
(\(y = \dfrac{1 + \tan x}{\sec x}\) ko pehle simplify karein phir derivative nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(y = \cos x + \sin x\) (kyun ke \(\frac{1}{\sec x} = \cos x\)), is liye \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos x - \sin x\).

book_ref.quote: the derivatives of the remaining trigonometric functions can be found using product rule and quotient rule of differentiation

blocks.prompt:
6 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(y = \cot x - \csc x\).
(Agar \(y = \cot x - \csc x\) ho to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\csc^{2} x + \csc x\cot x = \csc x(\cot x - \csc x)\). \((\csc x)' = -\csc x\cot x\) (minus ke saath).

book_ref.quote: the derivatives of the remaining trigonometric functions can be found using product rule and quotient rule of differentiation

(Curve \(y = \tan x\) ki \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) par slope nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The derivative of the sine function is the cosine function

(Agar \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\) aur \(g(x) = \cos x\) hon to \(f \circ g(x)\) aur \(g \circ f(x)\) nikalein. Kya yeh barabar hain?)
blocks.explanation: \(f \circ g(x) = \cos^{2} x + 1\); \(g \circ f(x) = \cos(x^{2} + 1)\). Yeh mukhtalif hain (\(x = 0\) par \(2\) aur \(\cos 1\)).

book_ref.quote: consider two real valued functions

(Agar \(x = 2t^{2}\) aur \(y = 4t\), \(t \ne 0\), hon to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Let a function be represented by parametric equations

blocks.prompt:
13 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(x = a\cos^{3} t\) and \(y = a\sin^{3} t\).
(Agar \(x = a\cos^{3} t\) aur \(y = a\sin^{3} t\) hon to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -3a\cos^{2} t\sin t\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3a\sin^{2} t\cos t\); taqseem se \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\tan t\).

book_ref.quote: Let a function be represented by parametric equations

(Agar \(x = t + \dfrac{1}{t}\) aur \(y = t - \dfrac{1}{t}\) hon to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Let a function be represented by parametric equations

blocks.prompt:
15 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(x^{3} + y^{3} = 3xy\).
(Agar \(x^{3} + y^{3} = 3xy\) ho to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(3x^{2} + 3y^{2}y' = 3y + 3xy'\) (right side par product rule); \(y' = \dfrac{y - x^{2}}{y^{2} - x}\).

book_ref.quote: Apply the Chain Rule to terms containing \(y\).

blocks.prompt:
16 Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) if \(y = \sin(x + y)\).
(Agar \(y = \sin(x + y)\) ho to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(y' = \cos(x + y)(1 + y')\); \(y'\) wale terms ikatthe kar ke \(y' = \dfrac{\cos(x + y)}{1 - \cos(x + y)}\).

book_ref.quote: Apply the Chain Rule to terms containing \(y\).

blocks.prompt:
18 Prove that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
(Saabit karein ke \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\), \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).)
blocks.explanation: \(y = \tan^{-1} x \Rightarrow \tan y = x\); implicit differentiation: \(\sec^{2} y\,y' = 1\), \(y' = \dfrac{1}{1 + \tan^{2} y} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\).

book_ref.quote: Proof method: write the inverse as a trigonometric equation, differentiate implicitly, change back to x.

book_ref.quote: The principal range decides the sign of every square root; this is why |x| appears in (v) and (vi).

book_ref.quote: Chain Rule forms: \(\frac{d}{dx}(\ln u) = \frac{u'}{u}\) and \(\frac{d}{dx}(\log_a u) = \frac{u'}{u\ln a}\).

(Stationary point ki definition likhein. \(f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 1\) ke stationary points nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: A point on the graph where its derivative is zero is called a stationary point.

(Function \(f: I \to \mathbb{R}\) ke global (absolute) maximum ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: \(f\) ka \(x = c \in I\) par global maximum hai agar tamam \(x \in I\) ke liye \(f(c) \ge f(x)\); \(f(c)\) global maximum qeemat hai.

book_ref.quote: is called global (absolute) maximum value of the function.

book_ref.quote: is called global (absolute) minimum value of the function.

(Second Derivative Test bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Agar \(f'(c) = 0\): \(f''(c) < 0\) ho to relative maximum, \(f''(c) > 0\) ho to relative minimum, \(f''(c) = 0\) ho to test inconclusive (koi faisla nahin).

book_ref.quote: \(f\) has relative maximum at \(c\) if \(f''(c) < 0\).
